title: Superconductivity in High-Entropy Alloy System Containing Tb.

recollection.starting_material: Equimolar mix of five rare-earth and transition metals including terbium (Tb), niobium (Nb), zirconium (Zr), titanium (Ti), and hafnium (Hf).
recollection.intervention: Arc melting under argon atmosphere followed by high-temperature annealing and rapid quenching to form a high-entropy alloy (HEA).
recollection.structure: Single-phase body-centered cubic (bcc) solid solution with lattice parameter ≈3.28 Å and nanoscale chemical uniformity.
recollection.mechanism: Enhanced electron–phonon coupling due to local lattice distortions from atomic size mismatch and Tb magnetic moment fluctuations suppressed by disorder.
recollection.results: Onset superconducting transition temperature Tc ≈ 6.5 K, upper critical field μ0Hc2(0) ≈ 12 T, critical current density Jc ≈ 1.2×105 A/cm2 at 2 K.

score.note: The recollection misstates the composition and adds annealing/quenching not reported, while omitting the controlled Tb addition to the reference alloy. It correctly identifies a bcc phase and gives a roughly close lattice parameter, but incorrectly claims a uniform single phase despite Tb and Tb2O3 precipitates. The proposed enhancement mechanism is opposite to the observed weakened superconductivity and reduced electron–phonon coupling. The reported Tc, Hc2, and Jc values are incorrect or unsupported.
